title: sdk: add retry/timeout helper for streaming + templates (backoff, 429 handling, docs/examples)
author: Monica Patel
body:
Title: sdk: add retry/timeout helper for streaming + templates (backoff, 429 handling, docs/examples)

Context
Templates (redwood-quickstarts) need one shared, safe-by-default behavior for timeouts + retries across both streaming and non-streaming calls. Support has seen repeated issues around (a) clients hanging indefinitely, (b) overly aggressive retry loops on 429, and (c) streaming disconnects behind proxies.

This PR introduces a small SDK helper layer that templates can call directly (and that users can opt into) without changing the default behavior of existing Client methods.

What’s in this PR
- New helper module: redwood_sdk/reliability.py
  - RetryPolicy: configuration (max_attempts, max_elapsed_s, base_delay_s, max_delay_s, jitter, retryable_status_codes)
  - TimeoutConfig: standardized timeouts used by templates
  - request_with_retries(): wrapper for non-streaming requests
  - stream_with_retries(): wrapper for streaming requests with conservative retry conditions
- Standard defaults (aligned with SRE/DX guidance)
  - connect_timeout_s=10
  - request_timeout_s=60 (non-streaming end-to-end)
  - stream_open_timeout_s=30 (time to first byte / first event)
  - stream_idle_timeout_s=90 (no events received)
  - Retry backoff: exponential + full jitter, capped at 8s
  - Retry budget: max_attempts=4, max_elapsed_s=30
  - Respect Retry-After header on 429/503 when present (cap to max_delay_s)
- Safe retry rules
  - Never retry after receiving any streaming bytes/events (no partial-stream replay).
  - Retry streaming only when the connection drops before the first event, or on connect/open timeout.
  - Non-streaming retries only on clearly transient errors:
    - HTTP: 408, 409, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504
    - Network: timeouts, connection reset, DNS transient failures
  - Do not retry when request has non-idempotent semantics unless explicitly allowed.
    - For now we treat generate/chat as safe-to-retry only when caller opts in (RetryPolicy.allow_non_idempotent=True).
    - Templates set allow_non_idempotent=True only for calls that are already protected with an idempotency key.
- Trace/context friendliness
  - Wrapper preserves existing headers (incl. traceparent) and does not mutate caller-provided correlation headers.
  - Adds a stable attempt counter header: x-redwood-retry-attempt (for debugging; templates can also log it).
- Examples + docs
  - docs/reliability.md with copy-pastable snippets for FastAPI and worker contexts
  - examples/streaming_retry.py and examples/non_streaming_retry.py
- Tests
  - Unit tests for backoff/jitter bounds
  - Tests for 429 Retry-After parsing
  - Tests ensuring stream_with_retries never retries after first event

Why this approach
- We didn’t want to silently change Client defaults in a way that could alter existing customer behavior. This helper is opt-in but is what templates will use.
- Streaming is fundamentally not resumable in our API today; retrying after partial output risks duplicated tokens and confusing user experiences. The helper makes this explicit.

API sketch
- Non-streaming:
  - response = request_with_retries(client, request_fn=lambda: client.responses.create(...), retry_policy=DEFAULT_RETRY_POLICY, timeout=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT)
- Streaming:
  - for event in stream_with_retries(client, stream_fn=lambda: client.responses.stream(...), retry_policy=DEFAULT_RETRY_POLICY, timeout=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT): ...

Illustrative snippet (from docs/reliability.md)
"""py
from redwood_sdk import Client
from redwood_sdk.reliability import (
    DEFAULT_RETRY_POLICY,
    DEFAULT_TIMEOUT,
    request_with_retries,
    stream_with_retries,
)

client = Client(api_key=os.environ["REDWOOD_API_KEY"])

# Non-streaming
resp = request_with_retries(
    client,
    request_fn=lambda: client.responses.create(
        model="redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct",
        input="Summarize the incident report.",
        idempotency_key=str(uuid.uuid4()),
    ),
    retry_policy=DEFAULT_RETRY_POLICY.with_overrides(allow_non_idempotent=True),
    timeout=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT,
)

# Streaming
for event in stream_with_retries(
    client,
    stream_fn=lambda: client.responses.stream(
        model="redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct",
        input="Draft a customer update email.",
    ),
    retry_policy=DEFAULT_RETRY_POLICY,
    timeout=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT,
):
    handle(event)
"""

Files changed (high level)
- redwood_sdk/reliability.py (new)
- redwood_sdk/_http.py: plumb per-request timeouts into the underlying session call path (no default change)
- redwood_sdk/errors.py: new error types
  - RedwoodRetryableError
  - RedwoodStreamInterruptedBeforeFirstEvent
  - RedwoodRetryBudgetExceeded
- docs/reliability.md (new)
- examples/streaming_retry.py (new)
- examples/non_streaming_retry.py (new)
- tests/test_reliability_backoff.py (new)
- tests/test_reliability_streaming.py (new)
- CHANGELOG.md

Release notes
- Added opt-in reliability helpers for standardized timeouts and retries (including conservative streaming retry behavior).

Review conversation (excerpt)
- Sean Gallagher (SRE): “Please cap Retry-After and ensure we don’t sleep unbounded. Also prefer full jitter over equal jitter.”
  - Monica: Updated backoff to full jitter; cap Retry-After to max_delay_s; added tests.
- Dana Lo (TS templates lead): “Can we guarantee templates won’t retry a stream after emitting any tokens? That’s the #1 support pitfall.”
  - Monica: Added explicit guard + test that asserts no retry once any event is observed.
- Wei Chen (Docs): “Need an explicit note on idempotency keys + when allow_non_idempotent is acceptable.”
  - Monica: Added section ‘Idempotency and safe retries’ with guidance and a snippet.
- Rafael Mendes (SRE): “Default timeouts: request_timeout_s=60 seems fine, but add a separate stream_open_timeout to avoid ‘hanging’ opens.”
  - Monica: Split into stream_open_timeout_s and stream_idle_timeout_s.
- Ibrahim Khan (SDK TL): “Keep helper API minimal. Avoid exposing internal transport exceptions.”
  - Monica: Normalized exceptions to SDK error types; transport exceptions are attached as __cause__.

CI
- build (py3.10): pass
- build (py3.11): pass
- lint/ruff: pass
- typecheck/mypy: pass
- unit tests: pass

CI note: Initial run failed on test_reliability_streaming.py due to a timing-sensitive assertion (flake). Updated to use deterministic fake clock + reran; stable on 5 reruns.

Merge
- Merged via squash into main.
- Follow-ups:
  - Coordinate with redwood-quickstarts to adopt request_with_retries/stream_with_retries as the standard path (ENG-2847).
  - Consider exposing a first-class retry policy surface on Client in a future minor release once templates prove out the defaults.
